chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated, from Ma'la ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him and said to him: 'Has Allah relinquished the matter to the servants?' He (AS) replied: 'Allah is Mightier than that.' I said: 'Then has He compelled them to sins?' He (AS) answered: 'Allah is more Just and better Judge than that,'

He then added: 'Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: O son of Adam, I am worthier of your good deeds than yourself, and you are worthier of your bad deeds than Me. You committed sins by means of My Power.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on divine decree and human free will regarding good and bad deeds?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the position between the two extremes), rejecting both absolute determinism (*jabr*) and total relinquishment (*tafwid*). By clarifying that humans commit sins using the divine power granted to them, the Imam establishes a nuanced balance where God remains the ultimate source of all capacity, yet humans bear primary responsibility for their moral choices, as reflected in the divine declaration: 'I am more worthy of your good deeds than you, and you are more worthy of your bad deeds than I.'

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 10. Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (RA) said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn `Amir said, on the authority of Mu`alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn `Ali alWashsha’ that Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (AS) said:

I asked him, “Has Allah relinquished matters to the servants?” He (AS) replied, “Allah is Mightier than that.” I asked, “Then has He compelled them to sins?” He (AS) answered, “Allah is more Just and better Judge than that.”

He then added, “Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: `O son of Adam, I am worthier of your good deeds than yourself, and you are worthier of your bad deeds than Me. You committed sins by means of My Power.’
